title: Blank Map: Outlines for Worksheets and Slides
description: Browse and download a Blank Map outline — countries, US states and regions with no labels, ready for worksheets, slides and colouring. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a teacher prints the blank US states outline on Monday, and by Friday the same sheet — coloured and labelled by hand — has taught the Midwest better than any atlas.
quick_answer: A Blank Map is an outline with borders and no labels — the starting sheet for worksheets, quizzes, slides and colouring. Browse world, country and US-state outlines here, download the clean version you need, and add your own labels, colours and questions on top.

A clean outline under your own annotations looks designed; a cluttered atlas scan looks borrowed. Business and school decks both benefit.
Filling a blank map from memory is the oldest active-recall trick in geography — far stickier than re-reading a labelled one.

faq: Are the outlines free to use in my classroom or slides?

They are provided for exactly that kind of educational and presentation use. If you plan to republish commercially, check the underlying map data attribution — the base outlines derive from open map data (OpenStreetMap contributors) whose licence asks for a credit line.
Can I get a map with no internal borders at all?
Yes — a silhouette-style outline (outer border only) is the cleanest base for cover slides and logos. Pick the country outline and the no-internal-borders style where offered.
Print and write, annotate in any slides or drawing app, or build the labelled version directly with the Custom Labeled Pin Map and Map with Legend tools on this site.
Why do Alaska and Hawaii move on US maps?
Inset convention: they are shifted and rescaled to fit the page beside the mainland. On a blank worksheet that is a feature — just do not measure distances from the insets.
Can I download at a bigger size?
Choose the largest export offered and print at that size; outlines are line art, so they scale cleanly compared with a screenshot of a street map, which pixelates.
The outlines show present-day boundaries. For older borders as study context, the Historical Map Context page is the honest companion — modern anchors for old maps, not a time machine.
Can I colour it on screen instead of printing?
Yes — Color a Map does exactly that in the browser, and exports your colouring as an image or a CSV list.
Is there a version with a grid or compass rose?
For print worksheets, the Printable Map with Scale Context page covers scale bars and print framing; a compass rose is best added in your document editor where you control placement.
